prompt: Write a Python function `parse_ini(text)` parsing INI text: '[section]' headers, 'key = value' lines (trim spaces), ';' comment lines and blank lines skipped. Returns nested dict {section: {key: value}}; lines before any section go under key ''. Duplicate keys: last wins. Example: '[a]\nx = 1\n' -> {'a': {'x': '1'}}. Return only the code.
test:
assert parse_ini('[a]
x = 1
y = 2
') == {'': {}, 'a': {'x': '1', 'y': '2'}}
assert parse_ini('; c
top = 1
[a]
x = 2
') == {'': {'top': '1'}, 'a': {'x': '2'}}
assert parse_ini('[a]
x = 1
x = 9
')['a']['x'] == '9'
assert parse_ini('') == {'': {}}

prompt: Write a Python function `word_search(grid, word)` where grid is a list of strings (rows of uppercase letters); return True if word can be traced moving up/down/left/right without reusing a cell, else False. Return only the code.
test:
g = ['ABCE','SFCS','ADEE']
assert word_search(g, 'ABCCED') is True
assert word_search(g, 'SEE') is True
assert word_search(g, 'ABCB') is False

prompt: Write a Python function `url_decode(s)` decoding percent-escapes (%XX hex) and turning '+' into space. Raise ValueError on a '%' not followed by 2 hex digits. Example: 'a+b%21' -> 'a b!'; '%2F' -> '/'. Do not use urllib. Return only the code.

Write a Python function `add_business_days(start, n)` where start is 'YYYY-MM-DD'; return the date n business days later (skip Saturdays and Sundays; start may be a weekend), as 'YYYY-MM-DD'. n >= 0. Example: add_business_days('2026-09-25', 1) (a Friday) -> '2026-09-28'. Return only the code.

Write a Python function `brace_expand(s)` expanding brace groups with comma options into all combinations in order: '{a,b}{c,d}' -> ['ac','ad','bc','bd']; 'x{a,b}y' -> ['xay','xby']; no nesting; a group of one item like '{a}' stays literal braces. No braces -> [s]. Return only the code.
test:
assert brace_expand('{a,b}{c,d}') == ['ac','ad','bc','bd']
assert brace_expand('x{a,b}y') == ['xay','xby']
assert brace_expand('plain') == ['plain']
assert brace_expand('{a}') == ['{a}']
assert brace_expand('{a,b,c}') == ['a','b','c']

prompt: Write a Python function `sudoku_valid(board)` where board is 9 strings of 9 chars ('1'-'9' or '.'); return True if every row, column, and 3x3 box has no repeated digit, else False. Return only the code.
test:
good = ['534678912','672195348','198342567','859761423','426853791','713924856','961537284','287419635','345286179']
assert sudoku_valid(good) is True
bad = list(good)
bad[0] = '334678912'
assert sudoku_valid(bad) is False
empty = ['.' * 9] * 9
assert sudoku_valid(empty) is True

prompt: Write a Python function `words_to_number(text)` converting English number words to an int, supporting 0-999999: 'one hundred twenty three' -> 123, 'twenty one thousand four' -> 21004, 'zero' -> 0, 'six hundred thousand' -> 600000. Input is lowercase, single spaces, optionally hyphenated ('twenty-one'). Return only the code.
test:
assert words_to_number('one hundred twenty three') == 123
assert words_to_number('twenty one thousand four') == 21004
assert words_to_number('zero') == 0
assert words_to_number('six hundred thousand') == 600000
assert words_to_number('forty-two') == 42
assert words_to_number('nine hundred ninety nine thousand nine hundred ninety nine') == 999999

prompt: Write a Python function `parse_md_table(text)` parsing a GitHub markdown table (header row, '---|---' alignment row, then data rows; cells trimmed) into a list of dicts keyed by header. Example input '| a | b |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |' -> [{'a': '1', 'b': '2'}]. Return only the code.
test:
t = '| name | age |
|------|-----|
| al | 3 |
| bo | 4 |'
assert parse_md_table(t) == [{'name': 'al', 'age': '3'}, {'name': 'bo', 'age': '4'}]
assert parse_md_table('| a | b |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |') == [{'a': '1', 'b': '2'}]
assert parse_md_table('| a |
|---|') == []
